events.title: The Universal Postal Union is founded
events.summary: Delegates from 22 countries sign the Treaty of Bern, creating a union for international mail.
events.description: On October 9, 1874, representatives of 22 countries meeting in Bern signed the Treaty of Bern, founding the organization now known as the Universal Postal Union. The anniversary is marked around the world today as World Post Day.
events.notificationTitle: The day the world agreed on mail
events.notificationBody: In 1874, delegates from 22 countries met in Bern and signed a treaty for international post.

sources.name: Swiss National Museum - The story of the Universal Postal Union

events.title: Kepler's Supernova is first sighted
events.summary: A brilliant new star appears in Ophiuchus, later named for Johannes Kepler.
events.description: On October 9, 1604, Italian astronomer Lodovico delle Colombo first observed a bright new star in the constellation Ophiuchus. Johannes Kepler, working in Prague, began observing it on October 17, and the stellar explosion is now known by his name.

sources.name: NASA - 420 Years Ago: Astronomer Johannes Kepler Observes a Supernova

events.title: The Washington Monument opens to the public
events.summary: Visitors can finally ride to the top of the obelisk honoring George Washington.
events.description: On October 9, 1888, the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., opened to the public after a steam elevator was installed. The obelisk had been completed in 1884 and dedicated in February 1885.

events.title: Uganda becomes independent
events.summary: Uganda ends British colonial rule, with Milton Obote leading the new government.
events.description: On October 9, 1962, Uganda gained independence from Britain. Milton Obote became prime minister at the head of a coalition between the Uganda People's Congress and Kabaka Yekka.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Uganda: The Republic of Uganda
EBSCO Research Starters - Uganda Gains Independence

events.title: Che Guevara is executed in Bolivia
events.summary: The revolutionary is killed at La Higuera a day after Bolivian forces capture him.
events.description: On October 9, 1967, the revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara was executed at La Higuera in Bolivia, a day after a U.S.-trained Bolivian army unit captured him. Declassified records show CIA involvement in the campaign against his guerrilla group.

sources.name: National Security Archive - Che Guevara and the CIA in the Mountains of Bolivia

events.title: The Wuchang Uprising begins
events.summary: A revolt in central China sets off the revolution that ends the Qing dynasty.
events.description: On October 10, 1911, an uprising broke out in Wuchang, part of present-day Wuhan in central China. It triggered the Xinhai Revolution, which overthrew the Qing dynasty and founded a republic, and the date is still commemorated as Double Ten.
events.notificationTitle: The revolt that ended China's last dynasty
events.notificationBody: An uprising in Wuchang in 1911 set off a revolution that toppled the Qing.

sources.name: Britannica Blog - The Wuchang Uprising on Double Ten (10/10/1911)

events.title: Fiji becomes independent
events.summary: Fiji gains independence 96 years to the day after it was ceded to Britain.
events.description: On October 10, 1970, Fiji became independent with dominion status. The date echoed October 10, 1874, when Fiji had been ceded to Great Britain.

sources.name: Parliament of the Republic of Fiji - Our Story

events.title: Cuba's Ten Years' War begins
events.summary: Carlos Manuel de Cespedes proclaims Cuban independence from Spain at his estate.
events.description: On October 10, 1868, planter Carlos Manuel de Cespedes proclaimed Cuban independence at his La Demajagua plantation near Bayamo, launching the Ten Years' War against Spanish rule. He freed his enslaved workers, who joined his rebel force.

events.title: The Outer Space Treaty enters into force
events.summary: The foundation of international space law takes effect.
events.description: On October 10, 1967, the Outer Space Treaty entered into force. Formally governing the exploration and use of outer space, the Moon, and other celestial bodies, it remains the foundation of international space law.

sources.name: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs - UNOOSA celebrates 50th anniversary of the Outer Space Treaty

events.title: The U.S. Naval Academy is founded
events.summary: A naval school opens at Fort Severn in Annapolis with 50 midshipmen.
events.description: On October 10, 1845, the Naval School opened at Fort Severn in Annapolis, Maryland, with 50 midshipmen and seven professors. Established through the efforts of Navy Secretary George Bancroft, it became the United States Naval Academy in 1850.

sources.name: United States Naval Academy - History of USNA

events.title: Apollo 7 launches the first crewed Apollo flight
events.summary: Three astronauts fly the first crewed mission of the Apollo program.
events.description: On October 11, 1968, Apollo 7 lifted off from Cape Kennedy with Walter Schirra, Donn Eisele, and Walter Cunningham aboard. It was the first Apollo mission to carry a crew.
events.notificationTitle: The flight that got Apollo back on track
events.notificationBody: In 1968, Apollo 7 carried the program's first crew into orbit.

events.title: The Second Vatican Council opens
events.summary: The Roman Catholic Church begins a council that will run until December 1965.
events.description: On October 11, 1962, the Second Vatican Council opened in Rome. Announced by Pope John XXIII, the council met in sessions until December 8, 1965.

events.title: The South African War begins
events.summary: War breaks out between Britain and the two Boer republics in southern Africa.
events.description: On October 11, 1899, the South African War, also called the Second Boer War, began between Britain and the Boer republics. The conflict lasted until May 31, 1902.

events.title: The Mary Rose is raised from the seabed
events.summary: Henry VIII's warship returns to the surface 437 years after it sank.
events.description: On October 11, 1982, the hull of the Mary Rose, Henry VIII's warship that sank in 1545, was raised from the seabed of the Solent after many years of searching, excavation, and recording.

sources.name: Mary Rose Trust - Raising the Mary Rose

events.title: Equatorial Guinea becomes independent
events.summary: The Central African nation ends Spanish colonial rule.
events.description: On October 12, 1968, Equatorial Guinea gained independence from Spain.
events.notificationTitle: A new nation on Africa's Atlantic coast
events.notificationBody: In 1968, Equatorial Guinea became independent from Spain.

sources.name: U.S. Office of the Historian - Equatorial Guinea

events.title: Rescuers bring 33 trapped Chilean miners to the surface
events.summary: The men emerge one by one after 69 days underground.
events.description: On October 13, 2010, rescuers began lifting 33 miners out of the San Jose gold and copper mine in northern Chile, 69 days after a collapse trapped them underground.
events.notificationBody: In 2010, 33 trapped Chilean miners were brought back to the surface.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Chile mine rescue of 2010

events.title: William of Normandy wins the Battle of Hastings
events.summary: Harold II is defeated and the Norman conquest of England begins.
events.description: On October 14, 1066, William, duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold II of England at the Battle of Hastings. The victory established the Normans as the rulers of England.
events.notificationTitle: The battle that made England Norman
events.notificationBody: In 1066, William of Normandy defeated Harold II at Hastings.

events.title: Chuck Yeager flies faster than sound
events.summary: The rocket-powered Bell X-1 becomes the first aircraft to exceed Mach 1 in level flight.
events.description: On October 14, 1947, U.S. Air Force pilot Chuck Yeager flew the Bell X-1 faster than the speed of sound over Rogers Dry Lake in California. The achievement was kept secret until June 1948.

events.title: Napoleon crushes Prussia at Jena and Auerstedt
events.summary: Two simultaneous French victories open the way to Napoleon's conquest of Prussia.
events.description: On October 14, 1806, Napoleon's forces defeated the armies of Prussia and Saxony in twin battles at Jena and Auerstedt. The victories let Napoleon complete his conquest of Prussia within six weeks.

events.title: China launches its first astronaut
events.summary: Yang Liwei orbits Earth aboard Shenzhou 5 on a 21-hour flight.
events.description: On October 15, 2003, Shenzhou 5 carried Yang Liwei, China's first astronaut, into orbit on a 21-hour spaceflight.
events.notificationBody: In 2003, Yang Liwei circled Earth aboard Shenzhou 5.

events.title: The Cassini spacecraft launches toward Saturn
events.summary: A long-lived mission to the ringed planet begins its journey.
events.description: On October 15, 1997, NASA's Cassini spacecraft launched on its long journey to Saturn, where it would study the planet, its rings, and its moons.

events.title: Munich holds the first Oktoberfest
events.summary: A royal wedding celebration in Bavaria begins what becomes a famous annual festival.
events.description: On October 12, 1810, the festival that became Oktoberfest began in Munich, celebrating the marriage of the Bavarian crown prince, later King Louis I, to Princess Therese von Sachsen-Hildburghausen.

events.title: Columbus's fleet sights land in the Caribbean
events.summary: After weeks at sea, Columbus's crew spots land in the Bahamas.
events.description: On October 12, 1492, land was sighted from the Pinta, ending the Atlantic crossing of Christopher Columbus's fleet, which had left Spain on August 3. The island, called Guanahani, is usually identified with San Salvador in the Bahamas, though the exact site is disputed.

events.title: Voskhod 1 carries the first multi-person crew into orbit
events.summary: Three Soviet cosmonauts, including a doctor, fly together for the first time.
events.description: On October 12, 1964, Voskhod 1 carried commander Vladimir Komarov, engineer Konstantin Feoktistov, and doctor Boris Yegorov into Earth orbit. It was the first spacecraft to carry more than one person, and Yegorov became the first doctor in space.

events.title: Philip IV orders the arrest of the Knights Templar
events.summary: The French king moves against the powerful military order and seizes its property.
events.description: On October 13, 1307, King Philip IV of France ordered the arrest of every Templar in France and seized the order's property there. The arrests made much of Europe aware of the crimes alleged against the order.

events.title: Construction of the White House begins
events.summary: A cornerstone is laid for the president's house in the new federal city.
events.description: On October 13, 1792, construction of the White House officially began with the laying of a cornerstone during a Masonic ceremony. Enslaved people worked alongside hired laborers at every stage of construction through 1800.

sources.name: White House Historical Association - Building the White House

events.title: Italy declares war on Germany
events.summary: Italy turns against its former Axis partner during the Second World War.
events.description: On October 13, 1943, Italy declared war on Germany. Marshal Pietro Badoglio read the declaration at Brindisi, and the document, signed by King Victor Emmanuel III, was sent to Berlin through the Italian Embassy in Madrid.

sources.name: The National WWII Museum - The Allied Campaign in Italy, 1943-45: A Timeline, Part One
Imperial War Museums - Italy declares war against Germany 1943

events.title: A U-2 flight photographs Soviet missile sites in Cuba
events.summary: Aerial reconnaissance captures the evidence that sets off the Cuban Missile Crisis.
events.description: On October 14, 1962, an American U-2 flight over Cuba took photographs that analysts studied over the following days. The images showed the Soviet Union building nuclear missile bases in Cuba, bringing the two superpowers into direct nuclear confrontation.

sources.name: U.S. National Archives - Aerial Photograph of Missiles in Cuba (1962)

events.title: The Gregorian calendar takes effect
events.dateNote: First day of the Gregorian calendar; adoption outside Catholic Europe came later.
events.summary: Ten days vanish from the calendar as Pope Gregory XIII's reform begins.
events.description: On October 15, 1582, the Gregorian calendar took effect. Proclaimed by Pope Gregory XIII to reform the Julian calendar, the change advanced the calendar by 10 days, so the day after October 4 was counted as October 15.

events.title: ThrustSSC breaks the sound barrier on land
events.summary: A British jet-powered car sets a land speed record of 763 mph.
events.description: On October 15, 1997, ThrustSSC set the world land speed record at 763 mph, becoming the first land vehicle to officially break the sound barrier.
